question.text: According to the workbook, which floating rate is given as the example for an Interest Rate Swap (IRS) in India?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes an interest rate swap as a contract where one party makes payments at a fixed rate and the other at a floating rate, and specifically cites the 3-month MIBOR as the example floating-rate benchmark used in India. The Trap: The US Prime Rate and 10-year US Treasury are USD benchmarks, not INR. The repo rate is a policy rate set by the RBI; it is not given by the workbook as the IRS floating-rate example. Note: Source - NISM-Series-XXI-B Portfolio Managers Certification Examination workbook (Sep 2025), p. 349.
